technical.summary: Mixed signals with short-term bullish momentum (RSI rising, supertrend, hull) offset by price below major moving averages and weak trend strength; moderate risk entry with limited sector tailwind.

fundamental.summary: No actionable signals detected across insider, institutional, government, lobbying, or retail channels; elevated earnings risk in 3.5 years warrants caution.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (20/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but mixed congressional activity (1 purchase vs 1 sale, small amounts) and absent news sentiment provide no confirmation.

risk.summary: Severe macro deterioration: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (343.2) indicates extreme market stress, rising DXY pressures multinationals, and recent CPI event compounds financial sector vulnerability.

debate.key_bull_argument: Short-term momentum (RSI rising, supertrend bullish, hull bullish) combined with extreme fear sentiment (20/100) and price near support (51.0064) creates a contrarian entry opportunity for swing traders.
debate.key_bear_argument: Severe macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis levels at 343.2, rising DXY), price below all major moving averages (EMA50, SMA50, SMA200), weak trend strength (ADX), and zero fundamental conviction make this a high-risk entry in a deteriorating environment.

decision.entry_rationale: Short-term momentum (RSI rising, supertrend bullish) and extreme fear sentiment (20/100) create a contrarian setup at support; however, severe macro deterioration and price below all major moving averages present unacceptable risk in current environment.
decision.primary_risk: Inverted yield curve, VIX crisis levels (343.2), and financial sector vulnerability create systemic downside risk that outweighs short-term technical bounce potential.
decision.agent_agreement: moderate — technical and sentiment agents bullish, but fundamental and risk agents strongly bearish with high confidence in bear case
decision.portfolio_note: Already 34 positions in Financials sector (17% of portfolio); adding L would increase concentration risk during macro stress period when sector correlation rises.
